record.paper_title: Answering open questions in biology using spatial genomics and structured methods
record.original_question: How fluid are individual clonal populations within a tissue, and can a clone contain spatially distinct subclones that occupy their own niches, such as metastatic subpopulations that separate from the original clone and acquire distinct molecular characteristics?

evidence.quote: it remains to be seen how “fluid” individual clonal populations are within a tissue. Are there definable subclones within a clone that occupy their own spatial niche? In the case of cancers, cells from one clone may metastasize to form their own population elsewhere. In what ways is this subclone distinct from the original?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a tissue modeled as a spatial domain populated by cells, where each cell carries a genotype/molecular state and belongs to a clonal lineage (the set of descendants of a common ancestor cell). Define a clone's "fluidity" as the extent to which its constituent cells move, mix, and change molecular state over time within the tissue, and define a "subclone" of a clone C as a maximal subset S ⊆ C whose members share additional distinguishing molecular characteristics not present throughout C. Address the following:

(a) Characterize quantitatively the fluidity of individual clonal populations within a tissue: develop a framework (using spatially resolved lineage tracing and molecular profiling data) that measures the degree of spatial dispersion, intermixing, and temporal turnover of clones in healthy and diseased tissues.

(b) Determine whether a clone can contain spatially distinct subclones that occupy their own niches; that is, identify conditions under which subclones form, become spatially segregated, and stably inhabit separate microenvironmental niches.

(c) For the specific case of cancer, consider a primary clone from which a subpopulation metastasizes to a distinct anatomical location. Characterize in what molecular, transcriptional, and phenotypic ways such a metastatic subclone becomes distinct from its originating clone, and identify which of these differences arise from niche-specific selection pressures versus intrinsic evolutionary divergence.
artifact.status_search_result: This is an open biological research question about clonal fluidity and subclone formation in tissues, including metastatic divergence. While many studies on spatial genomics, lineage tracing, and tumor heterogeneity address aspects of it, no definitive general answer exists; the question remains an active area of investigation.

status_evidence.title: Spatial genomics and clonal evolution review
status_evidence.snippet: Spatially resolved analyses are revealing clonal architectures and subclonal niches in tumors, but a comprehensive understanding of clonal fluidity and metastatic divergence remains incomplete.
status_evidence.claim: Clonal fluidity and spatial subclone characterization are active open problems in spatial genomics.
